item.title: Retired NYPD officer arrested after 'off with his head' post over Florida mosque expansion
item.description: Retired NYPD officer Rodolfo Mienert allegedly posted "off with his head!" on Facebook targeting a Pinellas County commissioner over a mosque vote.
item.content:encoded:
A retired NYPD officer living in Florida was arrested Monday after authorities say he made a social media post calling for the beheading of a Pinellas County commissioner who recently voted to approve the expansion of a local mosque.

Rodolfo Mienert, who now lives in St. Petersburg, allegedly commented on a Facebook post criticizing Pinellas County Commissioner Brian Scott for supporting a land-use change that would allow the North Pinellas mosque to expand.

According to the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office, the 68-year-old ex-officer called Scott a "Republican turncoat" before writing, "off with his head!"

Mienert posted this Facebook comment under the username "Rudy MineAllmine," according to an affidavit obtained by Fox News Digital.

OHIO MAN CHARGED OVER GRAPHIC THREATS TO KILL TRUMP, BEHEAD GOP LAWMAKER

The account's profile picture shows Bugs Bunny holding a revolver, while its bio reads, "...if I pissed off a libtard today, I'm happy!! no further reply!!"

The last post made by this account reposted a campaign video from Scott, accompanied with the message: "DO NOT vote for this person, he voted FOR a mosque."

Detectives traced the IP address of the account that made the post to Mienert, who later confirmed the account was his.

MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY POSTING GRUESOME DEATH THREATS AGAINST KRISTI NOEM, PAM BONDI ON SOCIAL MEDIA

Mienert told detectives he is "very vocal and not afraid to share his opinion" on political issues and said he called Scott a "turncoat" because of his vote to approve the mosque expansion.

Mienert also told detectives he had attended an Oct. 27 County Commission meeting where residents discussed the mosque issue at length.

During that meeting, he said he escaped New York to "beautiful Florida" and claimed the growing footprint of the mosque would damage the environment and make traffic worse.

Mienert was arrested and charged with one felony count of a written or electronic threat to kill, an offense that carries a maximum of 15 years in prison in Florida.

In a statement, Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri said that "threatening to cut off the head of a county commissioner because of his vote on a land issue is intolerable and we will strictly enforce the law against anyone who makes threats of this nature."

Mienert, who retired as a sergeant after 22 years with the New York Police Department, remains in the Pinellas County Jail, according to records reviewed by Fox News Digital. He is set to appear in court Tuesday afternoon.

item.title: Peter King's new book 'The Game' sparks debate over NFL's most significant figures across four decades
item.description: Peter King's new book "The Game" ranks Bill Belichick at No. 24 and Don Shula outside the top 25 on his NFL Mount Rushmore of significance..
item.content:encoded:
The list of premier NFL historians has for a long time included Peter King as a contributor, and his new book titled "The Game" is a journey that gives color to the growth of America's sport from the 1980s, when baseball and the NFL were still sports landscape peers to the current day in which football simply dominates.

King, the former Sports Illustrated writer and founding author of the Monday Morning Quarterback column, has delivered 40 chapters about King Sport.

"The Game" is a journey that details everything from the perfect NFL career authored by a Steelers' player not part of the early-day Super Bowl titles, to the rebirth of the New York Giants in the 1980s, to the painful last stand of Bill Walsh, to the sad end of Al Davis in 2007 – with much in between and beyond.

The book is a sprawling, colorful ride through four decades in forty chapters.

FOOTBALL LEGEND BILL BELICHICK ADDRESSES HALL OF FAME SNUB AND WHETHER IT WAS A 'POLITICAL' DECISION

Sitting down with the writer allowed me an opportunity to explain to King how wrong he was about his Mount Rushmore of Pro Football.

Fine, so I didn't actually tell a legendary scribe he's wrong about his stuff. But it's fair to say I probed him about the water cooler conversation segment of the book, which he patterned after Mount Rushmore.

Having known King for decades, I reminded him that Mount Rushmore has four presidents on its granite cliff and his Mount Rushmore boasts 100 people, then adds another 10 just because, then includes an honorable mention section.

"Armando," King retorts, without missing a beat, "as you know, I always wrote long."

Fair enough.

Time to prod.

King did not include either Bill Belichick or Don Shula among his top 20 names on his Mount Rushmore.

EX-PATRIOTS STAR ON WHETHER TOM BRADY COULD FACE SAME HOF FATE AS BILL BELICHICK: 'CRAZY TO THINK ABOUT'

Belichick, who has more Super Bowl championships than any other coach in NFL history, is No. 24 on King's mountain.

"Well, my Mount Rushmore is about the people who have been most significant in making the NFL the monstrous game and product that it is today," King explains. "So, like I have Joe Carr, former NFL commissioner, as the 4th most significant guy in pro football history.

NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL WILL NOT TESTIFY BEFORE CONGRESS AMID SCRUTINY OF PAST TESTIMONIES

"I think it's hard for somebody, unless you're absolutely like the best who's ever done it, for me to say that he's more important in football history than, say, Lamar Hunt, or Pete Rozelle, or John Madden or Vince Lombardi ... And those are guys I have, obviously, in the top 10.

"There are so many people, and I went through so many iterations of this, but I just tried to stick with the sort of the tried and true approach of people who were most responsible for this game being as gargantuan as it is."

Before this gets out of control, understand that King was a Pro Football Hall of Fame selector for decades and thought it was a mistake not to induct Belichick as a first-ballot candidate.

So he is not anti-Belichick, folks.

MANNY FERNANDEZ, CORNERSTONE OF DOLPHINS’ PERFECT 1972 SEASON, DEAD AT 79

Shula, the winningest coach of all time and the architect of the NFL's only undefeated Super Bowl champion, is outside King's top 25.

"I just don't think of Don Shula as a more important figure than the people I put above him," King said. "I think the reason is, and look, the undefeated season is obviously, that team is without peer in modern NFL history without any question. And that was an incredible accomplishment, especially because they beat some incredible teams in that season. They had a great year.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"But I think the way I kind of look at it, other than the number of wins, which is paramount, when I look at Don Shula, I am left asking the question, 'What other contributions to the game did he have that should put him higher on this list? What are they?'

"And I am left not convinced that he made the kind of contributions that guys like Madden and Lombardi made. This is more than just your win total. It has to do with everything you contributed to the game."

King is a good sport allowing me to thrust and riposte with him a bit. Any book that can set off such an exchange over football is worth the time.

item.title: 7 holiday shopping scams to watch for this season
item.description: Black Friday deals are already drawing scammers who use fake delivery notices and gift card payment requests to steal your personal financial information.
item.content:encoded:
Black Friday is still weeks away, but the holiday shopping season is already picking up. Stores are promoting early deals, our inboxes are filling with sales emails, and chances are you're already thinking about gifts for family and friends. Scammers are getting an early start, too.

Holiday shopping scams are designed to blend in with legitimate promotions and messages. A tempting discount could lead to a fake online store. A delivery alert might ask you to confirm your address or pay a small fee. And an email about a problem with your order could be an attempt to steal your payment information.

The tricky part is that these messages often arrive when you're already looking for deals or expecting packages. Before you click or enter your credit card information, here are seven holiday shopping scams to watch for and simple ways to protect yourself.

DO NOT CLICK FAKE 'ACCOUNT RECOVERY' AMAZON EMAIL

No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay, plus a downloadable checklist, now at CyberGuyLive.com.

During the holidays, it is normal to receive messages from unfamiliar stores. You may also be expecting several deliveries at once. Meanwhile, sales and shipping deadlines create pressure to act quickly. Scammers take advantage of those distractions. A fake message becomes more convincing when it matches something you are already expecting. That's why one of the best ways to avoid holiday shopping scams is to verify unexpected messages through a company's official website or app rather than responding directly.

You see a social media ad for a name-brand coat, popular gadget or designer handbag at 80% off. The photos look professional, and a countdown clock warns that the deal is about to expire. Big discounts happen during the holidays. However, unusually low prices on popular merchandise can signal a scam. Some fake stores collect your payment and send nothing. Others deliver cheap counterfeits or products that look nothing like the advertisement.

The Federal Trade Commission warns that scammers frequently use social media advertisements featuring popular products at unusually low prices.

Fake shopping websites can look remarkably convincing. Scammers copy brand logos, product photography and website layouts to make their stores appear legitimate. Sometimes, the biggest clue is hiding in the website address. A fake store might add words such as "outlet" or "sale" to a familiar brand name. Others use subtle misspellings or unfamiliar web addresses.

One important detail: A padlock icon or HTTPS connection does not guarantee that a shopping website is legitimate. It means the connection is encrypted. Scammers can use encrypted websites, too. When in doubt, type the retailer's official address into your browser or open its trusted app.

"Your package could not be delivered. Please confirm your address." Messages like this appear through text messages and emails, often claiming to come from the U.S. Postal Service, UPS or FedEx. Because you may have packages on the way, the message can seem believable. Scammers frequently direct you to a fake tracking page. There, they may ask you to enter your address, credit card number or other personal information. Some demand a small redelivery fee.

The Postal Service confirms that it does not charge a fee for redelivery. If a text claims you must pay USPS to receive your package again, treat it as a warning sign.

Another common scam involves an email claiming that your payment failed, your shopping account has been locked or a purchase needs immediate confirmation. Some messages go further. They claim someone made an expensive purchase using your account and provide a phone number to call if you want to cancel it. That number may connect you directly to a scammer. Once you call, the person may request your credit card information, ask for a one-time verification code or pressure you into installing remote-access software.

If you cannot verify the message through your account, contact the company's customer service department using contact information from its official website.

Gift cards make convenient holiday presents. Unfortunately, scammers also like them because the money can be difficult to recover once the card numbers and PINs are shared. A scammer may pretend to be a seller, employer or family member who urgently needs financial help. Some even claim to represent government agencies or utility companies.

A legitimate company might sell gift cards or accept its own gift cards for purchases. However, demands to buy gift cards and send someone the card numbers or PINs are strong signs of fraud.

The holidays are a popular time for charitable giving. Scammers know that emotional appeals can encourage people to donate quickly. Fake charities may use names that resemble familiar organizations. Others take advantage of natural disasters or heartbreaking stories to solicit donations. Some scammers impersonate legitimate charities and direct donations to fraudulent payment pages.

You can also consult the FTC's charity guidance before donating.

CHEAP ANDROID PHONES FOUND WITH MALWARE ALREADY INSTALLED

Online marketplaces and local resale groups can be useful places to find holiday bargains. However, they also attract scammers posing as legitimate sellers. A seller might advertise a popular item at an unusually low price, then demand payment before you can inspect it. Others try to move conversations away from the marketplace to avoid its protections. Fake payment confirmations and requests for additional shipping fees are other warning signs.

Remember that not every marketplace provides buyer protection. Check its policies rather than assuming it will refund a fraudulent purchase.

Avoiding holiday shopping scams starts with a few simple habits. These precautions can help protect your finances and personal information.

These habits help reduce your risk even when an advertisement or shopping website looks legitimate.

Even careful shoppers can encounter convincing scams. The important thing is to respond based on what actually happened.

Simply opening a webpage does not automatically mean your accounts have been compromised.

Acting quickly can improve your chances of limiting the damage.

Good habits are your first line of defense, but nobody spots every scam every time, especially during the busy holiday season. That's where reliable security software can provide an extra layer of protection. I recommend using strong antivirus software that helps detect suspicious websites, phishing attempts and malicious links before they put your personal information at risk.

Look for software that offers real-time protection against viruses, malware, spyware and ransomware. Some security solutions also include scam detection tools that can help identify fraudulent text messages, fake shopping websites and suspicious links. These features are particularly useful when scammers impersonate familiar retailers or delivery companies.

A built-in password manager is another valuable feature. It can generate and securely store strong, unique passwords for your shopping accounts. That helps reduce the risk of someone accessing multiple accounts if one password is compromised.

AI-powered scams are also becoming more convincing. Fake celebrity endorsements, manipulated videos and fraudulent holiday giveaways can make questionable offers appear legitimate. Some security products now include AI-powered scam detection and deepfake detection tools to help identify certain types of manipulated content. However, these capabilities vary by product, device and platform.

While security software cannot stop every scam, combining it with secure payment methods, account alerts and careful shopping habits can help protect your money and personal information throughout the holiday season.

I love finding a great holiday deal as much as anyone. But I've learned that the best way to avoid getting scammed is to be a little skeptical when something looks unusually attractive or demands an immediate response. Scammers are getting better at copying familiar stores and creating convincing messages. They're also using AI to make fraudulent offers look more believable. That's why I recommend checking purchases directly through retailers you trust and using security tools that can help flag suspicious activity. A few extra seconds of checking could save you a lot of trouble. The holidays should be about enjoying time with the people you care about, not cleaning up after a scam.

item.title: Americans urged to avoid dangerous border state despite US lifting shelter order
item.description: Officials have lifted a shelter-in-place order for Matamoros, a Mexican city across the border from Brownsville, Texas, but Americans are still being urged not to travel to the region.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. officials have lifted a shelter-in-place order for government employees in a Mexican border city, but Americans are still being urged not to travel to the area.

The order applied to U.S. government employees in Matamoros, a Mexican city across the border from Brownsville, Texas.

The U.S. Mission to Mexico said on Oct. 30 that the law enforcement activity that had prompted the order had subsided.

DEADLY SECURITY RISKS PROMPT UPDATED TRAVEL WARNINGS FOR 13 COUNTRIES

"The order for U.S. government employees to shelter in place has been lifted," officials said.

They noted that the Mexican border state of Tamaulipas, where Matamoros is located, remains under the State Department's highest-level travel advisory — Level 4 or "Do Not Travel" — due to terrorism, crime and kidnapping.

The shelter-in-place order came amid heightened security concerns following two arrests in Matamoros that prompted roadblocks across Tamaulipas, according to Mexican authorities.

In an Oct. 30 statement, Mexican officials identified one suspect as Axel Alfredo "N," the alleged second-in-command of the Gulf Cartel's Los Ciclones faction.

"The deployment is part of efforts to strengthen the operational presence of security forces, expand surveillance activities and improve authorities' response capabilities."

Americans were also urged to notify friends and family of their safety.

The warning follows a similar security alert issued in August.

At that time, U.S. officials temporarily suspended government activities and travel to Mexicali, another Mexican border city over 1,000 miles northwest of Matamoros.

The alert came after officials received information about a possible armed attack on law enforcement facilities by Los Rusos, a criminal group.

item.title: Mariners hire 36-year-old Jason Kanzler as new manager after disappointing season
item.description: The Seattle Mariners tapped 36-year-old Jason Kanzler as their 22nd manager after his three seasons leading Chicago Cubs player development.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Mariners have achieved their first big goal of the offseason: hiring a manager.

"Jason has the mindset, expertise, communication skills and intensity to help create a championship standard here in Seattle," Dipoto said in a statement.

Prior to joining the Cubs in 2024, Kanzler served as a coach for the Houston Astros at the major league level in 2022 and 2023. In 2022, when the Astros won the World Series, he served as a major league coach before becoming the assistant hitting coach in 2023.

item.title: Chris Cuomo says talking about politics makes it difficult for him to avoid violence
item.description: Chris Cuomo told Frank Luntz he wants out of political media, citing Mike Tyson's quote about getting punched in the face as his new mantra.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Cuomo has no interest in running for office like his father and brother. In fact, he says talking about politics on television has made it difficult enough to control his violent urges.

"Man, I run from office. I’m telling you, I would never, ever, ever, ever consider running for office," Cuomo told pollster Frank Luntz on his podcast. "But in fact, I’ll tell you what I’m considering: getting the f— out [of talking about politics]."

BOBBY BURACK: THE ANTI-WHITE RESISTANCE IS ALREADY BEGINNING FOR COOPER FLAGG

"Mike Tyson has turned out to be a prophet, which is already a perversity. But when Mike Tyson said, ‘Social media has made people forget that some things that you say will get you punched in the face.’

"And my desire to punch people in the face has gotten, it’s consuming me, Frank. I can’t handle this. I can’t handle the stupidity. I can’t handle what wins. I can’t handle what gets paid. I can’t handle what succeeds. I can’t handle it."

We understand that Cuomo was probably joking. But if anyone were to abandon a successful media career because of an uncontrollable urge to get violent, he would rank near the top of our list.

For background, Cuomo now hosts a cable news show on NewsNation.

The younger Cuomo brother has a long history of losing his temper.

item.title: Tiger Woods to redesign famed Long Island golf club that was rocked by prostitution scandal
item.description: Tiger Woods and TGR Design will redesign a scandal-plagued Long Island golf club closed since 2021, bringing new life to the Gold Coast region.
item.content:encoded:
Tiger Woods and his design firm are set to break ground on a new project, reviving a golf club that's been closed since 2021.

The 15-time major winner announced that he and his team will be redesigning the Tam O’Shanter Country Club on Long Island, roughly 10 miles away from where he won the 2002 U.S. Open.

The club was rocked by a scandal in the early 2010s when it was reported that members of the club took prostitutes and strippers to the club for golf outings. The property was sold in 2019 for a potential housing development project, but plans fell through after an arsenic discovery, and the club closed two years later.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

But Woods is planning on bringing the once-famed course back to life.

"The opportunity to create a new golf experience in the heart of Long Island’s Gold Coast, a region steeped in rich history, is tremendously exciting for our team," Woods said in a statement. "I have great memories of competing on Long Island, especially at Bethpage. This region has an extraordinary golf course architecture tradition, and we look forward to contributing to that legacy with a course that players can enjoy for generations."

"Bringing Tiger Woods and TGR Design to this beautiful and historic part of Long Island is a remarkable opportunity," Brookville Mayor Dan Serota said in a statement. "Combining the Gold Coast’s longstanding golf tradition with Tiger and his team’s skill and attention to detail makes this an exciting project for Brookville and the broader region."

JON RAHM OPEN TO ACCEPTING BROOKS KOEPKA-LIKE PENALTIES IN ORDER TO RETURN TO PGA TOUR AFTER LIV GOLF EXIT

Woods' TGR Design is partnering with The Armchair Collective, a private golf company that bought the land in September.

The project will include new practice facilities, a new clubhouse and a golf performance center.

"Long Island is home to some of the most celebrated golf courses in the country, and we're looking forward to contributing to the region's rich golf history," Woods said in an Instagram post.

Woods' return to the golf course remains to be determined - he has not played since the 2024 Open Championship. When he was arrested in March, he said he was "hoping to" play in April's Masters, but he ultimately missed the entire 2026 season.

item.title: NYC marathon runner, 24, dies just 2 miles from finish line after sending dad chilling texts
item.description: Rachel Apa's father says rhabdomyolysis killed the 24-year-old NYC marathon runner, who collapsed at mile 24 during her first-ever race Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
New York City marathon runner Rachel Apa died on Sunday after collapsing at mile 24.

Apa, 24, set out to run the world-famous race on Nov. 1 for the first time, along with more than 60,000 other runners.

The former Bucknell University Division I field hockey player had reportedly trained for the marathon for months. The New York Times reported details from the runner's parents, Michelle and Steve Apa, on Monday.

HEALTHY ATHLETE HAD NO SYMPTOMS BEFORE MANDATORY HEART SCREENING REVEALED HIDDEN DEFECT

Michelle Apa said she watched her daughter run by at mile 14 in Long Island City, Queens. She took a video of Apa looking strong, smiling and giving out high-fives before taking off again.

The runner's mother then headed toward the finish line, planning to wait for her daughter at mile 25 in Central Park.

Steve Apa was back home in Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, sending his daughter supportive texts at every mile as he tracked her in the New York Road Runners app.

Rachel Apa reportedly texted her father back at mile 18, saying, "Ow." And once again at mile 19, "Ow ow."

MYSTERIOUS DISEASE SENDING YOUNG, HEALTHY TEXAS WORKERS INTO KIDNEY FAILURE

At mile 23, Steve Apa texted, "Final stretch." Rachel Apa never responded again, according to The New York Times.

Spectator Michaela Nicholas reportedly witnessed Apa pass by in her matching green shorts and tank top near mile 24 in Central Park. She cheered Apa on with only two miles to go. Seconds later, at around 1:30 p.m., Apa collapsed.

Nicholas, who is a hospital social worker, ran over to help and declared that Apa did not have a pulse. After Nicholas’ fiancée called for a doctor, two people who claimed to be physicians hopped in, taking turns administering CPR. Nicholas said she held Apa’s hand the whole time.

The New York Road Runners, the marathon organizers, told the Times that marathon medical staff arrived soon after and used a defibrillator to try to revive Apa. Paramedics then arrived with an ambulance.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

After realizing Apa was not moving in the tracking app, Michelle Apa reportedly headed to her daughter's location. When she arrived, the ambulance transporting her daughter was pulling away.

Michelle Apa was taken to Mount Sinai Medical Center, where doctors worked to save Rachel Apa’s life for more than six hours. She was declared dead at around 9:40 p.m., according to the report.

Steve Apa told The New York Times that his daughter's cause of death was rhabdomyolysis, a rare muscle condition that occurs after injury, severe dehydration and overheating, or, most typically, excessive, high-intensity exercise without rest.

"It’s unfathomable," he said. "Perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old."

The condition, also known as rhabdo, causes the muscles to break down when over-exerted, which leads to muscle death, according to Cleveland Clinic.

When this disintegration occurs, toxic components of the muscle fibers can enter the circulatory system and kidneys, which can cause kidney damage, essentially acting as poison to the body.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Common signs of rhabdo include weak muscles, muscle stiffness and swelling, muscle pain and a change in urine shade, closer to a brown, red or tea color. It can also lead to nausea, dehydration and loss of consciousness.

Symptoms can range from mild to severe, typically developing one to three days after the muscle injury.

The condition is life-threatening, as physicians encourage listening to your body and seeking medical attention immediately.

"If you feel especially sore or tired during a workout, stop and rest," Cleveland Clinic recommends. "Don’t push yourself beyond safe limits."

"[Stay] hydrated and avoid getting overheated. Take breaks in the shade if you’re doing physical activity in the heat."

The New York Road Runners told the Times that the last marathon death occurred during a medical incident in 2024.

In a statement responding to Apa’s death, the organization said, "We are deeply saddened by the death of one of our runners following yesterday’s race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with the runner’s family, friends and the entire running community."

Fox News Digital reached out to the New York Road Runners and Apa's family for comment.

Rachel Apa was working as a product manager for an electrical component company while working on receiving her MBA at Charleston Southern University, according to the report.

She was running to raise money to fight Parkinson’s disease, in honor of her late grandfather.

On the Parkinson’s Champions fundraising website, Apa wrote what her grandfather meant to her.

"My grandfather was my role model growing up," she said. "He taught me to stay active, push my limits and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement."

"Later in life, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, and I watched as the disease slowly took away the freedom to move that he once loved so much. He passed away in 2022, but the lessons he taught me continue to drive me forward."

She added, "I'm proud to run with Parkinson's Foundation Champions to raise funds and awareness for research, better care and a cure."

Rachel Apa raised more than $22,000 and counting for the cause.

CHEFS NAME AMERICA'S BEST FAST- FOOD FRIED CHICKEN AND BISCUITS — AND ONE CHAIN STANDS ABOVE THE REST

The side item was available in the 1990s, and many locations stopped selling it in the early 2010s, with the last locations discontinuing it in 2020, according to multiple reports.

POPEYES BRINGS BACK POPULAR MENU ITEM FOR GOOD, AND NOT EVERYONE IS HAPPY

item.title: AOC campaign memo frames growth from progressive firebrand to national Democratic Party force
item.description: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's campaign memo reveals how she built a nationwide movement around economic populism after Trump's 2024 election victory.
item.content:encoded:
An internal strategy memo released by the campaign committee for Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N. Y.) and distributed to key allies makes the case that the lawmaker has evolved from a progressive firebrand into a formidable national political force.

The five-page document makes no mention of a potential 2028 presidential or Senate run. Instead, it urges stakeholders to view her record as that of one of the Democratic Party's most effective messengers for working-class voters.

Following President Donald Trump’s 2024 election victory, the memo states, Ocasio-Cortez launched an aggressive nationwide push to rebuild the party around economic populism and establish a broad movement for working families.

CARVILLE TORCHES DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS AS 'PACK OF FOOLS,' PRAISES AOC'S POLITICAL EVOLUTION

"Over the past two years, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez has built a record of success that extends beyond her own electoral victories," the memo reads. "The Congresswoman has emerged as one of the most powerful endorsements in the United States and New York State specifically. Candidates from rural districts and battleground seats see her as an asset for their general election campaigns."

The document highlights her fundraising reach, citing more than 2 million contributions totaling $38 million, an average donation of $17. 56, and over $3 million funneled to other Democratic candidates and state parties.

'SQUAD' RAKES IN RECORD $2.35M WHILE SLAMMING THE DOOR ON COP DONATIONS

Her small fundraising operation is unmatched in the House and rivals that of Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., the memo claims.

According to the document, Ocasio-Cortez’s strategy was shaped by post-2024 conversations with "Trump-AOC" split-ticket voters in her New York district, who expressed deep, cross-partisan frustration with a political establishment perceived as favoring corporate billionaires over ordinary workers.

BERNIE SANDERS ADMITS DEMOCRATS FAILED WORKING-CLASS VOTERS ON ECONOMICS, DRIVING THEM TO DONALD TRUMP

"As Democrats tried to understand why Trump had won again, Rep. Ocasio-Cortez argued that the path for the party to win back working class voters should be centered on economic populism, confronting concentrated wealth and power, and revitalizing American democracy," the memo states.

The memo points to race-altering endorsements in key primary and general election races across California, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Montana. It highlights Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign in Michigan and Sam Forstag’s Congressional primary victory in Montana as central case studies of her influence in rural and conservative-leaning areas.

AOC SIDES WITH BERNIE-BACKED PROGRESSIVE IN SENATE PRIMARY CLASH WITH SCHUMER ESTABLISHMENT

Forstag trailed significantly in the polls before joining Ocasio-Cortez and Sanders on stage at their "Fighting Oligarchy" rally in Missoula, Montana. Following her endorsement and appearance, he was able to erase the deficit and win the Democratic primary.

The document outlines a turning point following her unsuccessful bid for ranking member of the House Oversight Committee, alongside a March 2025 budget standoff in which Senate Democratic leadership accepted concessions during federal shutdown negotiations.

In response, Ocasio-Cortez shifted focus to taking her message directly to voters.

BERNIE SANDERS DISMISSES HALEY STEVENS, SAYS MICHIGAN RACE IS AGAINST THE 'BILLIONAIRE CLASS'

Speaking at a rally in Idaho, Ocasio-Cortez laid out the central thesis of her national tour:

"I want us all to understand that this constant pressure we feel in our lives—of the water rising up to our throats, the impossibility to afford anything easily, the fear of speaking up or being who we are in public, the bitter divisions driven more by online algorithms than the truth, the crumbling of our rights and protections— understand that this, right now, is what it feels like to be governed by billionaires," she said.

In the two years since, the memo states, Ocasio-Cortez has held large-scale rallies in purple, red, and blue places alike.

"She made race-changing endorsements in swing districts and deep-blue party primaries, as well as in her home base of New York City," the memo added.

item.title: Ex-Rep Justin Amash says Mike Rogers 'would be more dangerous in the US Senate' than Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Former Rep. Justin Amash suggested that former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers "would be more dangerous in the U.S. Senate" than Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
item.content:encoded:
Former Rep. Justin Amash — who announced on Monday that he did not vote for Abdul El-Sayed or former Rep. Mike Rogers in Michigan's U.S. Senate race — said he thinks El-Sayed would "be far less dangerous in practice than Rogers."

Rogers, a Republican candidate endorsed by President Donald Trump, is facing Democratic candidate El-Sayed in the widely-watched Senate contest.

"It goes without saying that I have major disagreements with both Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed, and neither one particularly likes me," Amash wrote in a thread on X. "I also don’t vote for 'the lesser of two evils.' I believe you should support a candidate only if you truly want the person to hold that office. I’ve already voted, and consistent with the above principle, I didn’t vote for Rogers or El-Sayed. But I do know which one would be more dangerous in the U.S. Senate — and it’s not even close."

ELECTION DAY 2026: VOTERS CAST BALLOTS WITH CONTROL OF CONGRESS ON THE LINE

Amash pointed to Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., as a political figure who resembles El-Sayed. Sanders has supported El-Sayed in the Senate race.

"To assess who is the greater threat to American freedom, let’s take a look at my time in Congress with Rogers and Bernie Sanders, who shares many of El-Sayed’s views and can serve as his stand-in," Amash wrote. "Several of Sanders’s key proposals, in my opinion, would be exceptionally bad for our country. But given the structure of our government, he’s in no position to get those ideas enacted and enforced.

"In contrast, Rogers is extraordinarily bad on all the issues on which an individual member of Congress may be the deciding vote. Again, these are issues like war powers, surveillance, privacy, the freedom of speech, criminal justice, and government oversight and accountability," he asserted. "In this world — the real world, not the imaginary one that partisan pundits on the right and left live in — Rogers poses a far greater threat to individual liberty and the Constitution than Sanders. Moreover, it’s not just that Rogers is awful here; it’s that Sanders is actually much better on these issues than the median member of Congress."

MICHIGAN VOTERS MAKE SURPRISING CROSS-PARTY CHOICES AS ROGERS, EL-SAYED RACE REACHES FINAL HOURS

Amash asserted that between Rogers and El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate would be "less dangerous."

"I think it’s fair to view El-Sayed as someone who mostly will follow in Sanders’s footsteps on policy and therefore will be far less dangerous in practice than Rogers," Amash wrote, adding in parentheses, "(Again, El-Sayed as a senator will do many things that are bad. The question addressed at length is not whether he’s good but simply whether he’s better on the whole than Rogers.)"

The Rogers and the El-Sayed campaigns did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on Tuesday.

MICHIGAN VOTERS WEIGH IN AFTER DEM REP HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP CANDIDATE

Amash, who served in the U.S. House of Representatives from early 2011 until early 2021, voted to impeach President Donald Trump in late 2019. While he served most of his congressional tenure as a Republican, Amash switched to Independent in 2019 and then to Libertarian in 2020.

He lost the 2024 GOP Michigan U.S. Senate primary to Rogers.

Rogers went on to lose the general election that year to Democrat Elissa Slotkin, who was a House lawmaker at the time.

Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., who lost the Democratic Senate primary to El-Sayed this year, shook up the 2026 general election when she endorsed Rogers on Sunday.

item.title: These college football coordinators will be the next big head coaches, according to 'Film Guy' Brooks Austin
item.description: Florida State's coaching search could target rising coordinators like Buster Faulkner, Kevin McGiven, or Glenn Schumann, says analyst Brooks Austin.
item.content:encoded:
In a surprising turn of events, Florida State recently fired its embattled head coach, Mike Norvell, after a 3-5 start to the season.

While his record would indicate it was long past time for him to hit the road, the shocking part of it all is the fact that FSU was willing to pay his exorbitant buyout, which is reported to be around $50 million when all is said and done.

This means one of the premiere coaching jobs in college football has suddenly, and perhaps unexpectedly, come open, and the Seminoles will be in the market for a new head coach in the coming months.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL COULD EXPLODE AS LINCOLN RILEY AND DEION SANDERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURE

Many expect the Noles to take a swing at a big, currently established head coaching name, but recent history shows that may not be the smartest play.

Some programs think they need to make a big splash hire, when in actuality, the best candidates are often the ones hiding in plain sight.

Take the Kentucky Wildcats, for example.

They fired Mark Stoops after a 13-year stint in Lexington, and instead of parking a Brinks truck in front of a seasoned veteran, they handed the keys to Oregon offensive coordinator Will Stein.

The results speak for themselves, as the Wildcats lead the SEC eight games into the season.

FORMER NFL QB PHILIP RIVERS HAS BECOME A SERIOUS OPTION FOR NC STATE OPENING AMID COLLEGE FOOTBALL CAROUSEL

All that is to say, who will be the next hot-shot coordinator to take a job like Florida State and become the greatest thing since sliced bread?

One man who has a few names on his list is college football analyst Brooks Austin.

Austin watches hours of tape a week and identifies the best units across the country, and when I asked him about who the next big name will be when scouring the coordinator ranks, he had more than a few options.

"I've always studied Buster Faulkner at Florida and loved what he's done," Austin says. "I loved what he did at at Georgia Tech."

While Faulkner was one of the hottest coordinator names in the country heading into October, the months of spooks and scares certainly did a number on the Gators' OC and his reputation among elite playcallers, something Austin admits.

"I think Buster... he's kind of gotten tipped off lately in, in this league. People are kind of figuring out what it is he's doing."

A name that might be flying under the radar but needs some more attention is Utah offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven.

"I watched what Utah does, and I'm like, 'This is fun, man,'" he says with a smile. "This is fun, that you're getting to a different play in a different way every single time you do it."

In his first year in Salt Lake City, McGiven has the Utes scoring nearly 39 points per game, and doing so with an innovative two-quarterback system.

Austin admits that, while he likes what he's seeing from Utah and McGiven, there is a chance if it doesn't work right away in one of the "big boy leagues," it could fall apart quickly due to the impatience of SEC fans.

"If an SEC school hired Kevin McGiven, and it didn't work out in like the first six weeks, are they gonna sit there and go, 'why did we hire this high school offense,'" asks Austin.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"If you do that, and you hire that at a bigger like like blue blood program, and it doesn't work, people are gonna be like, 'well, duh, he runs a high school offense?'"

For all the talk of the offensive side of the ball, there are a few defensive coordinators who have also caught Austin's eye.

"Glenn Schumann at Georgia, he's always been a guy that is like really, really smart, and is just such a great teacher of concepts, and is still really young."

Another one who fits the mold of young, innovative DC is Bryant Haines at Indiana, whom Austin calls "a lunatic" (that's a positive trait for a defensive coordinator, by the way).

One more name Austin mentioned is a guy who is flying way under the radar given his current employer, and that is Louisiana Tech DC Luke Olson.

"(Olson) is like 33 (or) 34 years old, and he is highly, highly respected," he mentions "Like when (offenses) go to face this guy, they're like, 'We got a tough one this week.'"

"Luke Olson's a dude."

Suffice to say, there are a lot of brilliant football minds in the college game right now, and although Florida State may go in a different direction, they can't go wrong taking a look at some of these names.

If the Seminoles want a "dude" at head coach, they know where to look.

item.title: Bird flu kills US resident after dairy cow exposure, marking nation’s third death
item.description: A Yakima County resident with underlying health conditions died after contracting H5N1 bird flu from infected dairy cows at a local dairy farm.
item.content:encoded:
A resident of Yakima County, Washington, has died from complications of bird flu, public health officials confirmed, marking a rare fatal human case of the virus in the United States.

The individual, who had underlying medical conditions, was hospitalized with severe illness after contracting avian influenza through exposure to infected livestock at a local dairy facility.

Local officials declined to release the person’s name, age or gender, citing privacy concerns.

H5N1 BIRD FLU CONFIRMED IN AUSTRALIA FOR THE FIRST TIME, MEANING VIRUS HAS NOW REACHED EVERY CONTINENT

"Our hearts go out to the individual's family and loved ones during this difficult time," Dr. Dave Atteberry, health officer for the Yakima Health District, said in a statement.

"Avian influenza can cause severe illness, particularly among people who have underlying health conditions," he went on. "While this is a serious and heartbreaking outcome, the risk to the general public remains low."

Health officials on Monday also confirmed a third human case of avian influenza in Yakima County. That individual, who was also exposed to infected dairy cattle at a local farm, has not been hospitalized and has not experienced severe illness.

Public health teams are actively tracing and monitoring close contacts of both individuals for potential symptoms.

RARE TICK-BORNE VIRUS TURNS DEADLY FAST AS US CASES REACH RECORD HIGH, EXPERTS WARN

"People at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus," the health district said in an advisory.

"If you work on a dairy farm and develop symptoms after potential exposure to infected cattle, contact your healthcare provider or the Yakima Health District."

Avian influenza, or bird flu, is a disease caused by influenza type A viruses that typically spread among wild aquatic birds and domestic poultry, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

In recent years, an outbreak of the H5N1 strain has expanded beyond birds to infect various mammals, including domestic dairy cows and outdoor livestock.

Federal and state health officials emphasize that the overall risk to the general public remains low.

Person-to-person spread of bird flu is extremely rare and has not been identified in the U.S., according to the CDC.

item.title: Missouri State Highway Patrol captures convicted murderer who escaped Tennessee prison
item.description: Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex last week before Missouri state troopers tracked down the escaped murderer.
item.content:encoded:
Missouri state troopers have captured an escaped convict who broke free from a Tennessee prison last week, a highway patrol spokesperson told Fox News Digital Tuesday.

Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Oct. 25, officials said previously. He was serving a life prison sentence for murder.

After his escape, he allegedly stole a truck, and authorities said they used FLOCK cameras to help track it down. As state troopers closed in on him, they say he tried to veer off the road and got stuck. 

He was arrested without further incident about two hours after police first caught wind of his possible location, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.

TENNESSEE INMATE CONVICTED OF MURDER ESCAPES FROM PRISON, STEALS PICKUP TRUCK, MANHUNT UNDERWAY: OFFICIALS

"On November 3, 2026, at approximately 9:30 a.m., the Patrol’s Missouri Information Analysis Center and Troop A Communications received information from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation that Morley may be traveling westbound on Interstate 70 near Independence," the Missouri State Highway Patrol said in a statement. "The suspect vehicle was located using FLOCK cameras, and officers began to deploy to the area. With additional use of FLOCK cameras, the suspect vehicle was located by undercover officers traveling south on Missouri 291 in Liberty."

SEND US A TIP

Police from several different local and federal agencies, including the Kansas City Police Department, Independence Police Department, Career Criminal Task Force, Homeland Security Investigations, and the United States Marshals Service, assisted in the effort to surround and capture him, MSHP said.

Staff at the prison noticed Morley was unaccounted for at around 11:30 p.m., and a review of surveillance footage subsequently revealed him crossing through the prison's perimeter fence. According to Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatch audio, Morley was last seen at the prison around 4 p.m. Sunday.

CONVICTED MURDERER GOT OVER 5-HOUR HEAD START AFTER PRISON ESCAPE BEFORE LOCAL POLICE WERE NOTIFIED: OFFICIAL

Morley was arrested in 2022 in connection with the murder of a man named Cody Birchfield. Police had initially arrested Morley near the border with North Carolina and later found Birchfield's body under Morley's home. In 2025, he was convicted at the end of a trial that included his ex-girlfriend testifying that, "he f---ing killed him."

Tennessee authorities later publicly thanked the public and the Missouri Highway Patrol for their help recapturing the killer, who was previously convicted of first-degree murder, burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism.

item.title: Idaho deer hunter reports Bigfoot encounter in remote woods after he 'smells the smell'
item.description: An Idaho deer hunter near St. Maries reported loud tree knocking, a deep gibberish voice, and an overpowering smell of death with no carcass found.
item.content:encoded:
An Idaho deer hunter out on an evening hunt a couple of weeks ago in the mountains near St. Maries has now heard the knocks and smelled the smell of what had to be a Bigfoot.

The hunter was minding his own business and walking down a trail on Tuesday, Oct. 20, around 5 p.m. when he first heard what he described to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization as "loud knocking on a tree."

The noises were coming from a creek bed about 200 to 300 yards away from him. While he didn't catch a glimpse of who or what was responsible for the knocking, he says it was "immediately followed by a super strong smell of death."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"The knocking persisted for 5-10 minutes, and upon searching for any carcasses producing the smell, nothing was found. I also heard briefly what sounded like a really deep voice but I couldn't make out what it was saying, sort of gibberish," the hunter reported to BFRO.

"I did not see any human footprints or any signs of people on that trail or in the general area. I was the only truck I saw all day on the road leading to the drainage I was in."

COUNTRY BOYS IN KENTUCKY HEAR KNOCKS IN WOODS AT NIGHT BEFORE ONE CATCHES GLIMPSE OF BIGFOOT WITH SPOTLIGHT

What else could it have been, but a Bigfoot? I've never seen a deep voice speaking in gibberish be reported before, but this is a veteran outdoorsman with no prior incidents of an encounter like this before.

He knows the woods. He knows the signs of a dead animal nearby, and he couldn’t explain what he encountered alone at dusk last month.

"The smell of decay was extremely strong, as if you were standing right on top of a carcass. It was overpowering," he added. "I could not even find a single sign of a dead animal near me."

item.title: Bruce Springsteen sparks fan fury after backing Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
item.description: Bruce Springsteen's endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race drew fierce backlash from fans citing antisemitism concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Bruce Springsteen has a message for Michigan voters — and some of his longtime fans aren't having it.

The rock legend faced criticism from some social media users after backing Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, prompting angry fans to accuse The Boss of crossing a political line.

Springsteen, who has never shied away from politics, took aim at President Donald Trump in his endorsement of El-Sayed, portraying the progressive candidate as a defender of American democracy.

"Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution, he’s a fighter for our American Democracy, and he’s a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House. That’s why I’m in his corner 100%. Bruce Springsteen," he penned on social media.

CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT

Critics questioned why the New Jersey-born singer was endorsing El-Sayed, given controversies over the candidate's political associations and positions on Israel.

"Bruce Springsteen, the guy who spent 40 years cashing in on ‘Born in the USA,’ finally posts after two years of silence just to call an elected American president ‘corrupt, lawless, and anti-American’ while locking arms with Abdul El-Sayed, the same guy who campaigned with Hasan Piker (the streamer who said America deserved 9/11) and still can’t shake the Muslim Brotherhood questions about his own family."

METALLICA FRONTMAN JAMES HETFIELD BLASTS ENTERTAINERS PUSHING POLITICAL AGENDAS AT CONCERTS

Another commenter criticized the singer's political activism, writing, "The Boss isn’t fighting for the Constitution. He’s just another rich coastal has-been who needs a new reason to hate the country that made him."

"Bruce Springsteen who performed at the concert for NY at MSG on 2001 after 9/11….. is now campaigning for a Muslim brotherhood sympathizer," another person wrote. "Did I not have this on my bingo card for today."

Another longtime fan expressed sadness and anger over what they viewed as Springsteen's failure to understand the impact of his endorsement on those who have long fought antisemitism.

"Shame on you. You are not educated to understand what your endorsement means to so many life long fans and good people that are fighting antisemitism and hatred for thousands of years. You are acting like an ignorant uneducated school child. You did this for what reason? This is so foolish. I’m so sad., I’m 59 years old.. Shame on me for thinking you were educated and smarter. Take the time to understand the other point of view."

However, not everyone was ready to turn on the rock icon.

EL-SAYED'S SILENCE OVER MOM'S FBI QUESTIONING RAISES TRANSPARENCY CONCERNS

Springsteen's endorsement drew support from El-Sayed backers, including one self-described frequent concertgoer who accused critics of unfairly targeting the Democratic candidate.

"As a huge Springsteen fan, and veteran of over 50 different shows around the country, and a resident of Michigan, and supporter of Dr. Abdul El Sayed, I support this message 100%. I suspect that some of your Jewish fans may have issues with this, but that's their problem. That just shows their bigotry. They're the first ones to … complain about the racism and bigotry of Maga, and yet here they are doing the same damn thing to Abdul. Anyway Bruce, thank you for supporting the good Dr. and always being on the side of the good guys."

"Fully with you, he's the man," one supporter wrote.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Thank you Bruce. History is about to be made. Abdul is more than qualified," another added.

Another commenter questioned El-Sayed's political beliefs and policy positions.

"Would love to know exactly what El-Sayed’s beliefs and what he is doing that American you love so much? America is not a socialist country nor is socialism the USA’s belief no matter who has been in the Oval Office."

Meanwhile, El-Sayed's Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., accused the Democratic candidate of misleading Michigan voters about his views on the Muslim Brotherhood, pointing to reported associations involving members of El-Sayed's family.

El-Sayed previously told Fox News that he has "never been" and will "never be" a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. Fox News Digital is not aware of any direct ties between El-Sayed and the organization.

Springsteen also released a second video message addressing election officials and government representatives, urging them to protect the integrity of the voting process.

"Hi, it’s Bruce Springsteen. I’m speaking to election officials and representatives of our government on election day. You have sworn an oath to preserve, protect, and defend our constitution."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

He continued, "That means you have a solemn duty to ensure that our votes are securely counted. Thomas Jefferson said, government requires the consent of the governed. You who represent us must never consent to any directives that undermine our constitutional right to a free and fair election. Our vote is our voice, and it’s up to you to ensure that our voice is heard. I wish you all a good election day, and thank you for your service."

The accompanying caption urged followers who had not yet voted to do so and directed them to OathProject.org to take what Springsteen described as an "Oath to the Constitution."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The endorsement comes as El-Sayed faces Rogers in a Michigan U.S. Senate race. El-Sayed, a former Wayne County health official, is running on a progressive platform centered on universal healthcare after defeating Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary.

The race has featured disagreements over U.S. support for Israel and accusations of antisemitism. Stevens endorsed Rogers, who is seeking a political comeback after losing the 2024 Senate race by fewer than 20,000 votes.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Springsteen and El-Sayed for comment.

Fox News Digital's Pedro B. Rodriguez-Aparicio and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: MS NOW host links Election Day to wiping out Pat McAfee and the 'manosphere'
item.description: Joe Scarborough used his "Morning Joe" Election Day rant to claim Pat McAfee is "ruining GameDay" and that voters could reject the "manosphere."
item.content:encoded:

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Now the MS NOW blowhard wants us to believe that American voters are declaring McAfee as public enemy No. 1, and they're voting for woke candidates as a "gotcha" to the GameDay host. That's quite a feather in Pat's cap.

item.title: Susan Collins' Maine Senate office vandalized with 'disturbing' graffiti on night before Election Day
item.description: Susan Collins' Biddeford, Maine, office was hit with red paint and the message "BLOOD on her HANDS," marking the second vandalism incident in a month.
item.content:encoded:
The Biddeford, Maine, office of Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, was vandalized Monday night for the second time in a month, Collins' chief of staff told Fox News.

After vandals previously spray-painted the building's door in September, saboteurs on Monday dumped a bucket of red paint in front of the location while writing in crimson — "BLOOD on her HANDS" — on the sidewalk in front of the building.

"This is another incident in a series and the second attempt at our Biddeford office to intimidate the Senator and her staff. These tactics are disturbing, but not effective. Our staff is undeterred and on the job," Collins' chief of staff Katie Brown told Fox News' Alexis McAdams.

TRUMP REAFFIRMS ICE ARREST POLICY AFTER CONFUSING GUIDANCE SPARKS ALARM AMONG AGENTS

The Biddeford office is near the scene of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer-involved shooting in which a law enforcement officer shot and killed 26-year-old Colombian national Johan Sebastián Guerrero in July.

Days after the shooting, protesters barged into the Biddeford office's front door, chanting "vote her out."

PERSONAL JABS, BILLIONAIRE DONORS AND PARTY LOYALTY FUEL HEATED MAINE SENATE DEBATE

In September, the "Trump whore" epithet was spray-painted in red on her office door.

Collins' challenger for her U.S. Senate seat, former Democratic state Senator Troy Jackson, condemned the vandalism in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. 

"There’s no place for this in Maine. Vandalism and intimidation are wrong, full stop. Senator Collins and her staff should be able to do their jobs without anyone defacing their office, and I condemn whoever did this," Jackson said.

Jackson had also condemned the September incident in another statement to Fox News Digital.

COLLINS INSISTS SOCIALIST RIVAL WON'T BEAT HER AS MAINE'S MONEY MACHINE: 'YOU'LL LOSE BIG TIME'

"Senator Collins and her staff should be able to do their jobs without anyone defacing their office, and I condemn whoever did this," Jackson said.

Biddeford police are investigating the incident, according to Collins' campaign.

Troy Jackson's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for further comment.
